champion: Metastatic Malignant Pleural Mesothelioma to the Tongue
ordered_diagnoses: Metastatic Malignant Pleural Mesothelioma to the Tongue

facts.raw_span: A 62-year-old nonsmoking man presented with multiple pleural thickenings and a marked effusion on the left side
multiple pleural thickenings and a marked effusion on the left side
nodular growth appeared on the mid third of the tongue
Nodular growth observed on the mid third of the tongue
Epithelioid solid formations with pseudopapillary structures
Immunoreactive for calretinin, AE1/AE3, D2-40, Wilms tumor protein 1
Absence of nuclear staining for BRCA1-associated protein 1
Negative for methylthioadenosine phosphorylase
Homozygous deletion of CDKN2A gene by fluorescent in-situ hybridization
Neoplastic subepithelial proliferation, consisting of epithelioid cells in the tongue
Neoplastic cells immunoreactive for calretinin, confirming mesothelial origin
The disease remained stable until July 2023

concepts.why: The patient presented with multiple pleural thickenings and a marked effusion, and pathological examinations revealed epithelioid solid formations with pseudopapillary structures, immunoreactive for calretinin and other mesothelial markers.

concepts.preferred_label: Metastatic Malignant Pleural Mesothelioma to the Tongue
concepts.why: The patient developed a nodular growth on the tongue, which was found to be a metastasis of the malignant pleural mesothelioma, as evidenced by the presence of neoplastic epithelioid cells immunoreactive for calretinin.
The absence of nuclear staining for BRCA1-associated protein 1 explains the BAP1-negative status of the Malignant Pleural Mesothelioma.

rationales.F01: Pleural thickenings and effusion suggest malignant pleural mesothelioma.
rationales.F05: Epithelioid solid formations with pseudopapillary structures are characteristic of malignant pleural mesothelioma.
rationales.F06: Immunoreactivity for calretinin, AE1/AE3, D2-40, and Wilms tumor protein 1 supports mesothelial origin.
rationales.F07: Absence of nuclear staining for BRCA1-associated protein 1 is consistent with BAP1-negative malignant pleural mesothelioma.
rationales.F09: Homozygous deletion of CDKN2A gene is a common genetic alteration in malignant pleural mesothelioma.
rationales.F11: Neoplastic cells immunoreactive for calretinin confirm mesothelial origin and support diagnosis of metastatic malignant pleural mesothelioma to the tongue.
